S6: [MAJOR] The group fan-out write path is outside every concurrency invariant -- evidence: 05-backend-schema.md:91-95 "Send atomicity. The recipient account's active `devices` rows are locked `FOR UPDATE` before the device-set comparison ..."; 05:120-122 "Queue cap. Under the `FOR UPDATE` lock of Send atomicity, after each insert the rows beyond the newest 1000 ..."; 05:109-112 "Nudge once. The empty-queue check and the envelope inserts run under the same `FOR UPDATE` lock on the recipient's device rows". `PUT /api/groups/{group_id}/messages` (02-TRD.md:74) makes no device-set comparison, and nothing in spec/ says it takes that lock, trims each member device to 1000, or nudges at all. The brief requires all three: "The nudge rule of feature 2 applies to each member account" (instruction.md:99; checklist C-CF-181), and "a device never holds more than 1000 waiting envelopes ... when requests arrive at the same moment" (:60, :279). Under 05 as written, a group send racing a one-to-one send to the same device can leave 1001 envelopes or send two nudges. No lock order is given across several member accounts, so two overlapping group sends can deadlock, which gives a 5xx that :501 forbids. Secondary: in the sign-in lockout statement (05:113-117), `locked_until = CASE WHEN locked_until < now() THEN NULL WHEN failed_sign_ins + 1 >= 5 THEN now() + interval '15 minutes' ...` resets the lock to a new fifteen minutes on every wrong password while the lock is active. Neither the brief ("refused for fifteen minutes", :74) nor 00:31 says this. fix: add a group fan-out invariant: lock every current member's active device rows FOR UPDATE in ascending id order, then run the empty-queue check, the inserts and the 1000 trim in that one transaction, and nudge after commit for each member account whose queues were all empty. In the lockout statement, add `WHEN locked_until > now() THEN locked_until` before the re-lock branch, or log the lock reset in 00 and state it in the brief.

S7: [MAJOR] The final self-test phase contradicts the spec's own delivered-seed invariant -- evidence: 06-implementation-plan.md:40-42 says "`/app/USER_README.md` lists the seeded logins; walk journeys 1 to 8 of 03". Journeys 4-8 in 03 (03-app-flow.md:76-93) sign in as `user@example.com`, `user2@example.com`, `user3@example.com` and `user4@example.com`. Along the way they register devices, which publishes profiles, save a recovery PIN, leave a waiting envelope for `nova` and create the group `Weekend Hike`. 05-backend-schema.md:145 says "When the build is finished the seeds are exactly as seeded (no device, profile, recovery record, group, waiting envelope or sign-in lock)", 00-decisions.md:70 says "trials use freshly signed-up accounts", and solution/checklist.md:425 C-DM-20 grades that state. Anyone who follows phase 11 as written fails that check. All other phases have exits and are now in dependency order, and phase 11 does use a detached start. fix: in phase 11, walk the journeys with freshly signed-up accounts (or on a throwaway database), and add to the exit: "the four seeded accounts still have no device, profile, recovery record, group, waiting envelope or sign-in lock".

D1: [BLOCKER] The brief never says a browser keeps its conversations after a reload or in a new tab, and the only rule about browser storage makes keeping anything optional -- evidence: line 139 (Core features 10.3) "Whatever Beacon keeps in this browser's storage between visits holds no readable message text, attachment bytes or profile names; it is encrypted under a key that only the account password unlocks." Line 107 (7.3) only requires the /unlock prompt "before anything from this browser's store is shown". Line 257 reduces LocalStore to "the encrypted browser store", while companion 13.6 says "the message store must be encrypted at rest" and 15.2 calls it "the at-rest-encrypted message database". Rule 1.6 deletes a message from the service once it is acknowledged, so the browser is the only place a conversation can live. The laziest build stores keys and sessions but keeps messages only in memory, and it meets every sentence: nothing readable is stored, the password is asked for, and /chats is empty after a reload. The graders already depend on persistence: tests/test_output.py:721 `second.goto("/chats")` then waits for the row ("the linked browser never listed the conversation before archiving", :725), and :798 `ben_tab.goto("/chats")` expects unread-count "3" (:803). Fix: state the obligation at the head of 10.3, e.g. "Each browser keeps its own conversations, messages, unread counts, contacts and settings between visits: after a reload or in a new tab, once unlocked at `/unlock`, `/chats` and every conversation show what they showed before, until a message is deleted, disappears by timer, or the browser signs out or is unlinked. What it keeps holds no readable message text, attachment bytes or profile names; it is encrypted under a key that only the account password unlocks." Rename LocalStore at line 257 'the encrypted message store in the browser'.

Author in judged_criteria: (1) criterion 'A message sent to a signed-out person puts a banner in the conversation saying why the message is stuck at Sending.' evaluation_rule 'Signing out from the devices page unlinks that browser, so an account signed out everywhere has no device to receive a message. (3) criterion 'A conversation at a laptop width fits a full screen of messages into a plain working view.' evaluation_rule 'Sign up two accounts in separate windows and trade about twelve short messages, then view the conversation at a laptop width. No if oversized padding, gaps or type leave room for only a few messages, or the view carries a hero band, feature cards, promotional drawings or marketing copy.' Fields: task completion, ui_visual, somewhat_important, 1, anchor conversation.working_view, facet layout, items [C-UX-59, C-UX-33]. Move C-UX-31 from R4.items to R3.items, and end R3's no sentence with ', or drawn in the same blue as the rest of the page.' Widen R9: criterion 'The German, Arabic and Greek home pages show the hero, the four feature cards and the statement bands in their own languages.' RC-04: R16 and pytest both claim C-CF-188, and R7's typeface clause repeats the Inter assertion -- C-CF-188 is in R16.items (grounding.yaml l.1202) and in the golden_trajectory step 'sealed message reaches the recipient devices only' (l.435). pytest-provenance also cites it for test_browser_store_holds_no_readable_text_and_asks_to_unlock. But cycle 2 ordered the split, and channel_lint.py cannot see this double claim: it only flags deterministic ids the rubric claims and ids both a browser substep and the rubric claim. R7's 'the type reads as a clean, friendly sans-serif' / 'the type looks technical or ornamental' (C-UX-54, l.1088) repeats test_type_scale_phone_tilt_and_self_hosted_fonts l.232-247, which pins the Inter stack. Yes if a readable line inside the dialog tells the person that no account has that username. Yes if neighbouring sections are told apart by a faint change of ground tint and generous spacing rather than ruled lines, and each drawing accompanies a heading and text. No if thin rules or borders divide the sections, two sections run together with no visible break, sections are set apart by strong blocks of colour, or a drawing stands where copy belongs.' R7 items become [C-UX-58, C-UX-47, C-UX-32]. Re-class C-UX-54 ui->capability under test_type_scale_phone_tilt_and_self_hosted_fonts.

RC-07: R13 and R4 use words their rules never define -- R13's rule says 'the Beacon ring glowing like a lamp' (grounding.yaml l.1163), but only R5 says what the ring is (instruction.md l.324: a circular speech-bubble glyph drawn as a ring with a small tail). R4's 'an outgoing bubble inside a drawing' (l.1048) never says which drawn bubbles count as outgoing. R12's 'readable time' is also undefined; the R12 rewrite under RC-09 fixes that. Fix: in R13's rule, replace 'and the Beacon ring glowing like a lamp' with 'and the ring-shaped speech bubble from the Beacon wordmark glowing like a lamp'. In R4's rule, replace 'or on an outgoing bubble inside a drawing' with 'or on the blue message bubbles drawn on the hero chat phone'.

RC-08: R12 cannot be decided cold, and R8, R13, R15 and R24 never say how to reach a conversation -- the judge signs in with seeded credentials. The seeded accounts ship with no device, conversation or group (instruction.md l.285), so it lands either on an empty chats list or, once the workflows have registered nova's browser, on /link. R12's rule (grounding.yaml l.1151) gives no setup, so 'every conversation row shows ...' is either vacuously true or unanswerable. On a +5 critically_important criterion that means free points or a silent zero for every app. R13 ('The sticker picker in a conversation'), R8 ('the Send button in a conversation'), R15 ('then open a conversation') and R24 ('a group conversation') each need a conversation or group, and no rule says how to make one. Fix: use the R12 rule under RC-09. Give each of the other four its own setup sentence, worded differently so G52 sees no repeated sentence: R13 'Reach the picker by starting a chat with the username juniper from New chat on the chats list.'; R8 'For the conversation, open New chat on the chats list and start one with the username sol.'; R15 'A new account has an empty list, so first start a chat with wren from New chat, then return to the chats list and open that conversation.'; R24 'Make the group with New group on the chats list from any name and the usernames juniper and sol.'

RC-09: R12's rule leaves a raw timestamp and an empty list in neither case -- yes needs 'a readable time', but no fires only when a row 'lacks any time' (grounding.yaml l.1151). A row showing 1789571274000 is neither yes nor no, and so is an empty list. Fix: R12 evaluation_rule 'The chats list is the signed-in screen listing every conversation, and a new account starts with none. Sign up two accounts in separate windows, send one message from the first to the second, then open the chats list of the first. A readable time is a clock time, a day or a date a person takes in at a glance. Yes if the row shows the other username or profile name and a readable time for that message. No if the row lacks the name, lacks a time, or shows the time as a raw number such as a millisecond timestamp.'

RC-09: R23's yes and no cases overlap -- a dialog that lists near matches only after the full username is typed meets the yes clause 'shows search results beyond the exact typed username'. It also meets the no clause 'shows no account names before a full username is entered and never asks for contacts' (grounding.yaml l.1289). Fix: replace R23's no sentence with 'No if the dialog never shows an account name other than the one typed and never asks for contacts.'

RC-11: R4 can fail a correct app, and R1 asks for an arrangement the brief never gives -- instruction.md l.205 says 'pressed states and gradient stops use two mid, vivid blues' and 'the gradient stops inside drawings are the only other blues'. RC-12: R18 grades three facts a program can compute -- focus order is the sequence of activeElement bounding boxes, a visible ring is a computed outline or box-shadow on focus, and 'links show an underline when focused' is computed text-decoration-line. test_language_dialog_traps_focus_and_restores_control already walks Tab (test_output.py l.301-306), and test_reduced_motion_stops_shared_transition already hovers the Help link (l.395-404). The owner's rule is that the rubric grades only non-deterministic things. Cycle 2 raised this, and it was not applied. Fix: delete R18. Re-class C-UX-11, C-UX-26 and C-UX-36 ui->capability. In test_home_images_named_and_text_meets_contrast, Tab from the top of the home through #brandNavbar and assert three things for each focused element: the left edge moves right; outline-style is not none with width of at least 1px, or box-shadow is not none; and top bar links carry an underline in text-decoration-line or a bottom border, both when focused and when hovered. In R18's place, author the judgment half of C-UX-28: criterion 'Each phone render and feature card drawing on the home page carries a spoken name describing what that drawing shows.' evaluation_rule 'A spoken name is the text a screen reader announces for a picture, read from its alt text or aria-label. The two phones show a group video call of faces and a one-to-one chat; the four feature drawings sit above Say Anything, Speak Freely, Make Privacy Stick and Get Together with Groups. Yes if each of the six names describes its own drawing. No if a name is a bare word such as image, phone or illustration, a file name, or describes a different drawing.' Fields: task completion, accessibility, somewhat_important, 1, anchor home.image_names, facet a11y, items [ui half of C-UX-28].

RC-12: the obligations moved out of the rubric were re-classed and cited, but no assertion checks them, so nothing grades them -- pytest-provenance cites: C-UX-40 and C-UX-41 for test_phone_viewport_menu_button_reveals_links, which never uses the FULL_HD viewport it imports (test_output.py l.21; conftest.py l.116); C-UX-44, C-UX-51, C-UX-52, C-UX-65 and C-UX-66 for test_reduced_motion_stops_shared_transition, which reads no pulse colour, easing, card lift or .get-app colour; C-UX-45, C-UX-46 and C-UX-48 for test_home_images_named_and_text_meets_contrast, which reads no muted-paragraph or border colour and never presses a button; C-UX-60 and C-UX-61 for test_safety_numbers_match_and_identity_change_blocks_send, which only calls is_enabled to decide whether to click (l.1611-1624); C-UX-53 and C-UX-55 for test_voice_message_call_ringing_and_read_receipt, which reads no time styling. Fix (tests stage, then re-run G28 and G39): add the assertions. For C-UX-40 and C-UX-41, the container is wider at 1300 than at 1100, the same width at 1408 and FULL_HD, with equal side margins. For C-UX-44 and C-UX-52, only pulsate uses ease-in-out, and the Sending status pulses in a mid cool neutral. For C-UX-45 and C-UX-46, check the hue and lightness of a muted paragraph's colour and a border colour. For C-UX-48, the mouse-down .get-app background is a darker blue than at rest. For C-UX-51, hovering a feature card gives a negative translateY and a changed shadow or opacity. For C-UX-53, message times carry tabular-nums. For C-UX-55, a message time renders at 16px on a 22px line. For C-UX-60 and C-UX-61, a blocked composer-send is disabled with a cue beyond colour, and rest, hover and active styles differ. For C-UX-65 and C-UX-66, the .get-app background is the brand blue. Move C-UX-56 and C-UX-57 to test_type_scale_phone_tilt_and_self_hosted_fonts, asserting that .get-app's computed border-radius and box-shadow blur are below those of the card holding the first feature-illustration. R2 evaluation_rule becomes 'The feature cards are the four boxes titled Say Anything, Speak Freely, Make Privacy Stick and Get Together with Groups. Answer yes when all four are white, float on a faint, soft shadow with softened corners over a light grey band, and carry a simple flat drawing above the title. Answer no when any card is tinted or grey, flat with no shadow, heavily shadowed, square-cornered, photographic or without a drawing, or when the cards sit on a band that is not light grey.'
